demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.heading: The bench for Rs 0: its tests, and a scripted model
demos.purpose: Before you spend a rupee, run the bench where nothing can be billed. First its tests, 21 of them in evals/tests/test_prompt_bench.py. They answer with the kit's own generate() over a scripted model and stand-ins for the lane, and they check what step 4 claimed: each row's pool is read once and held fixed, the level and the temperature are sent and nothing else changes, generator.py is never written, every answer is judged by the gate's rule, and the rupees are list price. The one test that runs the recorder on google-genai's own types needs that library, which Module 0 installed in your venv. Before you spend a rupee, run the bench where nothing can be billed. First its tests, 21 of them in evals/tests/test_prompt_bench.py. They answer with the kit's own generate() over a scripted model and stand-ins for the lane, and they check what step 4 claimed: each row's pool is read once and held fixed, the level and the temperature are sent and nothing else changes, generator.py is never written, every answer is judged by the gate's rule, and the rupees are list price. The one test that runs the recorder on google-genai's own types needs that library, which Module 0 installed in your venv. Then the bench itself. The cell below runs prompt_bench.main(), the function make bench runs, over generator.py imported in your shell, with two things stood in. /v1/passages returns the handbook's first six clauses, cut by the kit's own chunker as the kit's tests cut them, so NP-03 is [Source 1] and LV-07 is [Source 4]. The model is a script behind generator._client. It writes five wordings of an answer to jn-03 in turn, the same five at every level and temperature, and "thinks" 120 tokens at LOW and 900 at HIGH, the numbers the kit's tests script. Its fifth wording has all 50 days encashed, so that you can see a failure printed. It also counts the thinking level and the temperature each call was sent with. The cell runs the bench twice: the two levels with --show, then a temperature of 2.0.

demos.heading: Five calls to /v1/query, judged by the gate's rule
demos.purpose: Now the real model, through the API. /v1/query is the request make eval-live sends for every golden row, and the bench's kit arm at LOW reproduces it, so these five answers are five more draws from what step 7 measures. The cell asks the way the gate asks, run_eval.ask() with top_k 6 as documind-ui-sa, and judges each reply with row_verdict() after reading the ledger's current versions from GET /v1/sources, as the gate does. It starts with /version, which names the model, the prompt version and the answer cache. The cache is off unless a deploy turned it on (SEMANTIC_CACHE, lesson 6.2); with it on, a repeated question can come back from the cache with no model call, and the five would not be five draws.

demos.heading: make bench: five runs at LOW and five at HIGH
demos.purpose: The bench on your lane: jn-03's pool read once from your /v1/passages, then generate() five times at LOW and five at HIGH, interleaved, each answer judged and priced. --show adds the pool and each level's distinct answers, the most frequent first. --report keeps every answer, the config it was sent with, its usage and its verdict in evals/reports/bench-levels.json, which the kit's .gitignore keeps out of git. The bench imports generator.py in your shell: Module 0 installed rag-api's pins in your venv, and if this shell lacks one the bench names it and stops before any call.

demos.heading: Change it: send a temperature of 2.0, and read what went out
demos.purpose: generator.py sends no temperature; the bench can. --temperature 2.0 adds a second arm, edit: the kit's prompt, the kit's level and a temperature of 2.0 on every call. The kit arm runs beside it, interleaved, so the two share the lane's conditions, and both print one prompt sha256, because the text is the same: the only difference the run can show is the knob. Without --levels the bench runs at LOW, so this run's kit arm is a third sample of the request steps 6 and 7 already asked. The table cannot prove that 2.0 was sent: it prints each arm's settings, not its requests. The recorder's log can. Every call in the report carries its config as sent (the thinking level, the temperature, None when none was sent, and the cap) and what came back.

The cell reads the rows written since T0, the time you noted in step 3, oldest first, with each row's tokens and the price cost.py gave it. Wait a minute after step 8, because a row can take a little while to reach the log, and if this is a new shell, set T0 again to a time before step 3.

A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors. The pin back is a separate window on purpose: pasted together with the line above, it would put acme straight back on RAG Engine before the lesson began. Leave it until the lesson's last step is done.
